newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Ocean Tankers plans to rejuvenate tanker fleet.
newsitem.headline: Ocean Tankers plans to rejuvenate tanker fleet.

text.p: Ocean Tankers Pte Ltd, one of Singapore's major private oil tanker companies, is planning to rejuvenate part of its fleet of about 90 tankers, a company source said on Thursday.
"Rejuvenation is in our plan. But it's not in our plan to raise the tonnage unless there is a need," the source said.
"We will continue to use existing ones if (they) can perform as good as new or newer ones. The important thing is (they have) to be efficiently run."
Ocean Tankers is a sister company of Singapore's leading private oil trading company Hin Leong Trading Pte Ltd.
The company had previously expanded its fleet of coastal and long-range tankers, bringing its total tonnage to about 2.5 million.
During 1996, Ocean Tankers acquired three long-range tankers of between 90,000 and 120,000 tonnes to facilitate its growing business of shipping oil products from the Middle East and to East Asia.
"Sometimes cargoes can only work to the east if the size is substantial," he explained.
Ocean Tankers' fleet of coastal tankers were also rapidly expanded over the past few years to take advantage of the growing intra-Asia trade.

The source said it has about 19 new coastal tankers of between 7,500 and 13,000 tonnes which are primarily used to service its regional trade. The tankers are also chartered out to major oil companies.
"We saw that there are more requirements for coastal lots and we expanded out fleet," the source said.
The company is also looking into upgrading and rejuvenating its bunker fleet to meet new regulations set out by the Port of Singapore Authority (PSA).
"We have to at least follow or keep up with the requirement so that we don't lag (others)," he said.
Hin Leong is the largest independent bunker supplier in Singapore.
The source said it was meaningless to give an average age for it's fleet as many of if its smaller tankers are brand new while the larger ones are fairly old.

The company's fleet is made up of five very large crude carriers, six long range tankers (between 80,000 to 120,000 tonnes), eleven medium range tankers (30,000 tonnes) and about seventy coastal and bunkering barges.
